Sales Chat - Getting Started

What it knows, what only you can tell it, and how to get a real answer out of it.
CLAUDE.AI PROJECT · ACTIVE SINCE 2026-09-17

Open it

Sign in at claude.ai with your @k12sta.com email. Sales Chat is in your Projects list. Start a conversation in it the same way you would any other chat - it already has the context it needs loaded.

AreaWhat you can ask
Our productsWhat each one does, which Skyward platform it needs, who in a district owns the problem it solves.

The four things only you can tell it

Nothing it can research will answer these, and it will ask you for them rather than guess:

  1. Which Skyward platform the district is on - SMS 2.0 or Qmlativ.
  2. What they already run of ours.
  3. Any live thread - an open case, a quote, a renewal. "None open" is a real answer.
  4. Anything you must not say - a lost deal, an unresolved escalation, a person who left. "Nothing flagged" is a real answer.
Why it leaves these blank instead of guessing. If you do not supply them, a briefing ships with those fields visibly empty and marked for you to fill. That is on purpose. A guess printed on a page you are holding in front of a customer is worse than a blank.

Skills: you have to ask for them by name

Skills are the reusable tools that build finished things - a briefing, a report, an SOW, a checklist. Inside a Project they do not start on their own. Name the one you want, or describe the outcome and let it pick.

Say thisYou get
"Power map [district] for me" or "there's a user group in [state]"sales-power-mapping builds a briefing you can carry into the room
"Write this up as a report"sta-html-report produces a branded HTML file
"Turn this into an SOW"sow-writer
"How do we compare to [competitor]"vendor-evaluation
If it ever tells you a skill cannot be run from a Project, that is wrong. Say so and ask it to call the skill by name. Tell Adam if it keeps happening.

Two rules it follows on every draft

  • No signature block. Drafts end at the sign-off line, because Gmail adds your signature automatically. One in the draft arrives twice.
  • No meeting offer unless you ask for one. It will not add "happy to jump on a call" to anything.

What it will not do

It will not invent pricing, contract terms, SLAs, support policy, or whether a product works with a given Skyward version. It will not tell you a district is an existing customer, because it cannot see Salesforce. When the honest answer is "I don't know," it says so and names who does.

Try these first

1. "I'm meeting with [district] next week. What should I know before I walk in?"
2. "A business official told me it's not in this year's budget. What's actually going on and what do I say?"
3. "Draft a follow-up to a tech director who went quiet after a demo three weeks ago."
4. "Which fund would a district use to buy time clocks, and why does that matter?"
